transcript: Contemporary musical theatre sounds like Christian rock. And every time I talk about this, I get a bunch of people in my comments blaming Pasek and Paul. And y'all, Pasek and Paul are a product of multiple trends. They are not the cause. On one hand, you have the rise and absolute dominance of the BFA Belt, which is just a singing technique that allows people to sing these pop and rock scores with the kind of resonance that you wanna hear on that style of score. Right? You don't wanna hear somebody try to sing so much better from legally blonde in an operatic style. This is also the direct results of scores getting higher. If you look at the belt of Ethel Merman, who had a much more distinct voice, she only ever had to hit up to like a C5. If you look at the score to Wicked, Elphaba has to hit multiple F5s, which, if you don't know music notation, that is significantly higher. And so in order to sing a role like Elphaba, you have to have a very healthy belt. You also have to have the range to be able to hit those notes. And even then, Elphaba still destroys a countless voices. Why does Elphaba not have an alternate? And then on the other hand, you have the fact that when you get these big inspirational moments in shows where the entire chorus is coming together and they're singing some Something to inspire you, like you will be found or if we make it through the night from Lost Boys. That It's structured very similarly to contemporary Christian rock in terms of what it's trying to do in terms of the build of the song. This is not a new phenomenon in musical theatre. What is new is the Christian rock of it all, because Christian rock as a genre is relatively new. Like, it really didn't explode in popularity until the 1990s and early 2000s and was quickly adopted by the church because of how effective it was at getting you to feel feelings. But musical theatre and these inspirational moments in musical theatre have always sounded like worship music. It was just gospel. Like, you can go through the entire musical theatre canon and in most shows, find at least one heavy gospel song, whether this is Blow, Gabriel Blow in Anything Goes or Brotherhood of man in how to succeed, sit down your rock in the boat in guys and dolls. The most famous song from the first musical ever is literally a spiritual. Even barbershop quartets, like in Music Man, are southern gospel. And sometimes it's just one or two of these moments, and then sometimes you get a score like, obviously godspell, but also Pippin. Have you listened to Pippin? That is all religious music, so it only makes sense. Like, gospel as its own genre really transformed into rock and pop Rock. It only makes sense that musical theatre going on a similar journey to have more pop and rock scores would have these songs that ultimately sound like Christian rock. And to be clear, I have no issue with the style of writing or singing. I love an inspirational moment in a musical. What I do have an issue is the way that the audience will critique artists that come into these roles that don't have this traditionally clear belt. Think like the criticisms that artists like Reeve Carney has gotten in Gatsby or Jordan Tyson in Hades Town because they don't sound like the original counterparts that I have an issue with. I do have an issue with the fact that scores are becoming higher and higher and harder to sing and less accessible to different and unique voices. I am also lamenting the trend towards having more big songs in musicals and losing these smaller moments. It's the evolution from having Dear Evan Hansen with a song like so big, so small and to break in a glove to then Greatest Showman that is just 100% bangers and there's no quiet moments. Even a song like tightrope has this big belted ending to it that I don't necessarily need from every single song in a show. I also don't love that when we do get these quieter scores like a Kimberley Akimbo, people complain that the scores aren't memorable enough because they don't have these catchy inspirational worship Style hooks to them, but that's a whole other story. I want more musical theatre that has a more dynamic score, that has the big belted moments, but also has room for the weird character actor that gets to sing a weird character song. That's.
